feature.title: AI tools that check the theology of worship songs: SongTheology and Asaph
feature.why: Original reporting dated inside the window about two working ministry tools: SongTheology scores worship lyrics against a seven-part theology grid (scriptural grounding, doctrinal clarity, God-centeredness, gospel presence, clarity versus ambiguity, congregational usefulness, pastoral durability; out of 35), and Asaph tracks theological and emotional balance across a church's setlists and syncs with Planning Center. Both run on Claude. It helps worship leaders, many without Bible training, put Christ-centered songs in front of congregations, and it carries its own built-in caution from a worship researcher. Not in topic memory (only Kairos/Transform Iran covered). Writer note: drop all place names from the source; the AI model is Anthropic's Claude, so disclose plainly if the publication has any relationship to Anthropic.

wisdomConcern: Outsourcing discernment: an AI score can tempt worship leaders to skip their own prayerful study of Scripture and pastoral judgment. The tool only reads lyrics, not the music or how a song is heard, and is not endorsed by any church body, so it should prompt deeper reflection, not replace it (as researcher Mark Porter warns).
